findings.title: sideEffects field marks all component source as side-effectful
findings.description: package.json declares sideEffects: ['**/*.css', 'src/components/**/*.ts', 'dist/components/**/*.js', 'dist/shared/**/*.js']. This tells bundlers that every component file has side effects, which completely defeats tree-shaking. When a consumer imports a single component via the barrel export (e.g., import { HelixButton } from '@helixui/library'), the bundler cannot safely eliminate unused components because it believes they all produce side effects. The per-component entry points in 'exports' mitigate this somewhat, but only if consumers use them directly. The sideEffects list should be restricted to only files that truly have side effects (customElement registrations).
findings.impact: All consumers using barrel imports get the entire library bundled regardless of usage. Defeats the primary tree-shaking optimization for npm consumers.
findings.fix: Change sideEffects to either `false` (if all side effects are handled by entry points) or restrict to only the files that call customElements.define(). Each component's index.ts that re-exports the class AND registers the element is side-effectful, but the barrel index.ts re-exports should not be. Consider: `"sideEffects": ["**/*.css", "dist/components/*/index.js"]`

findings.title: querySelector called inside render() method
findings.description: The render() method calls this.querySelector('[slot="caption"]') on every re-render to detect whether a caption slot is populated. This forces the browser to walk the light DOM subtree synchronously during each render cycle. For tables that re-render frequently (e.g., on sort or selection changes in a parent data-table), this adds unnecessary overhead.
findings.impact: Synchronous DOM traversal during every render cycle. Compounds with parent data-table re-renders.
findings.fix: Track caption slot presence via a @state() property updated in a slotchange handler, similar to how hx-card tracks _hasImage, _hasHeading, etc.

findings.title: Global document listeners registered unconditionally in connectedCallback
findings.description: Three global document listeners (click, pointermove, pointerup) are registered in connectedCallback and only removed in disconnectedCallback. This means while the color picker is in the DOM (even when closed/inactive), every mouse move and click on the entire page triggers these handlers. For pages with multiple color pickers or frequent pointer activity, this creates unnecessary overhead. The pointerMove handler runs on every mouse movement across the entire document.
findings.impact: Document-level pointermove handler fires on every mouse movement on the page. Multiplied by number of color picker instances in DOM.
findings.fix: Register pointermove and pointerup listeners only when a drag operation begins (on pointerdown on the grid/sliders), and remove them on pointerup. The document click listener should only be active when the picker popover is open. This pattern is already correctly implemented in hx-dropdown, hx-select, and hx-popover.

findings.title: Large row lists rendered with .map() instead of repeat() directive
findings.description: The _renderDataRows() method uses Array.map() to render table rows. Without the repeat() directive and stable keys, Lit cannot efficiently reuse DOM nodes when rows are reordered, inserted, or removed. For tables with hundreds of rows (the component warns at 500+), this means full DOM recreation on every re-render instead of targeted updates.
findings.impact: Full DOM recreation of all row elements on every sort, filter, or page change. Significant for tables with 50+ rows.
findings.fix: Use repeat() directive with a stable key function: repeat(displayRows, (row, i) => row.id ?? i, (row, pageIndex) => html`<tr>...</tr>`);

findings.title: Option list rendered with .map() instead of repeat()
findings.description: The _renderOptions() method renders the dropdown options using Array.map(). When the option list changes (e.g., filtering, dynamic loading), all option DOM nodes are recreated instead of being efficiently reused.
findings.impact: All option DOM nodes recreated on every option list change.
findings.fix: Use repeat() with option.value as the key.

findings.title: Filtered option list rendered with .map() instead of repeat()
findings.description: The combobox renders its filtered options using Array.map(). As the user types and the filter changes, the entire option list DOM is recreated on each keystroke. With debouncing at ~150ms, this means frequent full re-renders of potentially large option lists.
findings.impact: Full option list DOM recreation on every filtered keystroke. For lists with 100+ options, this creates significant GC pressure.
findings.fix: Use repeat() with a stable key: repeat(filtered, (opt) => opt.value, (opt, index) => html`...`);

findings.title: ~200 lines of color conversion utilities inlined in component file
findings.description: The hx-color-picker.ts file is 964 lines, with approximately 200 lines dedicated to color parsing and conversion functions (hexToRgb, rgbToHsv, hsvToRgb, rgbToHsl, parseColor, formatColor, etc.) defined at module scope. These utilities are tightly coupled to this single component.
findings.impact: ~5KB minified added to the component's bundle. Cannot be tree-shaken separately from the component.
findings.fix: Extract color utilities into a separate file (e.g., hx-color-picker/color-utils.ts). This improves code organization and, combined with proper sideEffects configuration, allows bundlers to exclude these utilities when the color picker is not imported.

findings.title: Typeahead timeout not cleared in disconnectedCallback
findings.description: hx-menu uses a setTimeout for typeahead buffer clearing (_typeaheadTimeout) but has no disconnectedCallback to clear it. If the menu is removed from the DOM while a typeahead timeout is pending, the callback will fire on a disconnected element.
findings.impact: Orphaned timer fires on disconnected element. Poor lifecycle hygiene.
findings.fix: Add disconnectedCallback: override disconnectedCallback(): void { super.disconnectedCallback(); clearTimeout(this._typeaheadTimeout); }

findings.title: MutationObserver watches subtree with attributeFilter
findings.description: The MutationObserver in hx-tabs observes the entire subtree for attribute changes on 'panel' and 'name'. While the attributeFilter limits which mutations are reported, the observer still monitors every descendant element for attribute changes. For tabs with rich panel content (forms, tables, etc.), this means the observer fires on any element in the subtree that happens to have a 'name' attribute changed (e.g., form fields). Each mutation invalidates the tab/panel caches and re-syncs.
findings.impact: Cache invalidation and re-sync triggered by any 'name' attribute change in descendant content, including form fields.
findings.fix: Use childList observation on the host (not subtree) to detect when tab/panel elements are added or removed, combined with subtree: false.

findings.title: setTimeout in _show() not tracked or cleared on disconnect
findings.description: The _show() method uses setTimeout(() => { document.addEventListener('click', ...) }, 0) to defer registering the outside-click listener. This timer is not stored in a class property and cannot be cleared in disconnectedCallback. If the popover is removed from the DOM immediately after opening, the callback will register a document-level click listener with no cleanup.
findings.impact: Orphaned document-level click listener if component is removed during the microtask window.
findings.fix: Store the timeout handle and clear it in disconnectedCallback.

findings.title: offsetWidth/offsetHeight read on every pointermove during drag
findings.description: The _onPointerMove handler calls _getHostSize() which reads this.offsetWidth or this.offsetHeight on every pointer move event during a drag operation. These layout property reads force the browser to perform a synchronous layout calculation at 60+ fps.
findings.impact: 60+ forced layout calculations per second during drag. Causes jank on lower-end devices.
findings.fix: Cache the host size at the start of the drag (in _onPointerDown) and reuse throughout.

findings.title: Recursive DOM traversal via _getVisibleItems() on every keydown
findings.description: _getVisibleItems() recursively walks all children to build a flat list of visible tree items. This is called on every keydown event (ArrowUp, ArrowDown, etc.) and also in _handleSlotChange. For trees with hundreds of items, this recursive traversal on every keystroke creates noticeable latency. The method has no caching.
findings.impact: O(n) recursive DOM walk on every keyboard navigation event. Compounds with deep nesting.
findings.fix: Cache the visible items list and invalidate it on slotchange and expand/collapse events. Store in a @state() property that is rebuilt only when the tree structure changes.

findings.title: _selectedValuesSet getter creates new Set on every access
findings.description: The _selectedValuesSet getter creates a new Set<string> from the values array on every access. This getter is called multiple times during render to check whether each option is selected. For a combobox with 100 options, this creates 100 new Set instances during a single render pass.
findings.impact: N * Set constructor calls per render where N is the number of options. Creates GC pressure.
findings.fix: Cache the Set as a @state() property and rebuild it only when the values array changes (in willUpdate).

findings.title: _filteredOptions getter re-filters on every access during render
findings.description: The _filteredOptions getter re-runs the filter logic on every access. It is called multiple times during render. The filter involves string comparison (toLowerCase, includes) on every option for each access.
findings.impact: Redundant O(n) filtering on each getter access during render.
findings.fix: Cache filtered results in a @state() property, updated in willUpdate when the filter query or options change.

findings.title: window.matchMedia called on every open/close animation
findings.description: The _getAnimationDuration() method calls window.matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)') every time the drawer opens or closes. Other components (hx-carousel, hx-counter) correctly cache the media query result.
findings.impact: Unnecessary MediaQueryList object allocation on each animation.
findings.fix: Cache the prefers-reduced-motion MediaQueryList and listen for changes.

findings.title: _reducedMotion getter calls window.matchMedia on every access
findings.description: The _reducedMotion getter at line 87 calls window.matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)').matches on every access. This is called in updated() whenever the open property changes. While not high-frequency, it creates a new MediaQueryList object each time.
findings.impact: Unnecessary MediaQueryList allocation on each open/close cycle.
findings.fix: Cache the result as a class property and update via a change listener on the MediaQueryList.

findings.title: querySelectorAll scans all cells on every keydown event
findings.description: The _handleKeydown method calls shadowRoot.querySelectorAll('[part~="td"],[part~="th"]') on every keydown event. For a table with 500 rows and 10 columns, this queries 5000+ elements on every arrow key press.
findings.impact: 5000+ element query on every keyboard navigation event in large tables.
findings.fix: Cache the cell list and invalidate it only when rows/columns change.

findings.title: Calendar day cells rendered with .map() instead of repeat()
findings.description: The date picker renders its calendar grid cells using Array.map(). When the user navigates between months, all 42 day cells (6 rows x 7 columns) are recreated instead of being efficiently updated in place.
findings.impact: 42 DOM elements recreated on every month navigation.
findings.fix: Use repeat() directive with the date ISO string as key.

findings.title: Multiple querySelector calls in _updatePosition()
findings.description: The _updatePosition() method performs three querySelector calls (.trigger-wrapper, [part="tooltip"], [part="arrow"]) every time the tooltip position needs to be recalculated.
findings.impact: Three DOM queries on every tooltip reposition.
findings.fix: Use @query decorators for cached references.

findings.title: querySelector for slot element on every mouseleave event
findings.description: The _handleTriggerMouseleave() method calls this.shadowRoot.querySelector('slot:not([name])') on every mouseleave event.
findings.impact: DOM query on every mouseleave for a static element reference.
findings.fix: Cache the slot reference using @query or a firstUpdated initialization.

findings.title: Document click and keydown listeners always active
findings.description: hx-split-button registers document-level click and keydown listeners in connectedCallback that remain active even when the dropdown menu is closed. While both handlers early-return with 'if (!this._open) return', they still fire on every document click and keydown, running the open-state check. For pages with many split buttons, this multiplies.
findings.impact: Two document-level event handlers per split button instance, firing on every click and keydown on the page.
findings.fix: Register document listeners only when the menu opens (_openMenu) and remove them when it closes (_closeMenu). This follows the pattern used by hx-dropdown.

findings.title: _updateAriaMetadata walks up entire ancestor chain on every connect and slotchange
findings.description: _updateAriaMetadata() walks the entire parent chain (parentElement loop) to compute nesting level, then queries all siblings to compute posInSet/setSize, and calls closest('hx-tree-view') to check selection mode. This runs on connectedCallback and every slotchange of the children slot. For a tree with 100 items, this means 100 parent-chain walks on initial render.
findings.impact: O(depth) parent walk + O(siblings) query per item on connect. For 100 items at depth 5, this is 500+ parent traversals on mount.
findings.fix: Have the parent hx-tree-view propagate level, posInSet, and setSize to children via properties or data attributes rather than having each child compute its own. Alternatively, debounce the metadata update to batch it after all items connect.

findings.title: getBoundingClientRect called on every pointermove during color grid drag
findings.description: The _handleGridPointerMove and _handleHueTrackPointerMove methods call getBoundingClientRect() on every pointermove event during drag operations. This forces a synchronous layout calculation 60+ times per second.
findings.impact: Forced layout 60+ times per second during drag.
findings.fix: Cache the bounding rect at the start of the drag (on pointerdown) and reuse during the drag.

findings.title: getBoundingClientRect called on every pointermove for half-star calculation
findings.description: The _handleMouseMove method calls getBoundingClientRect() on every pointer movement to determine whether the user is hovering over the left or right half of a star.
findings.impact: Forced layout on every mouse move over the rating component.
findings.fix: Cache the star element rects on mouseenter of the rating component and clear on mouseleave.

findings.title: size property uses reflect: true but only drives CSS class
findings.description: The 'size' property on hx-counter has reflect: true, meaning every size change writes the attribute back to the DOM element. The size value is only used to set a CSS class in the classMap directive inside render().
findings.impact: Unnecessary DOM attribute write on every size property change.
findings.fix: Remove reflect: true from the size property unless external CSS selectors target [size] attributes.

findings.title: All 12 properties use reflect: true
findings.description: Every @property on hx-image uses reflect: true. Properties like sizes, srcset, and border-radius do not benefit from reflection. Each reflected property performs a DOM attribute write on every change.
findings.impact: 12 DOM attribute writes on every property batch update.
findings.fix: Remove reflect: true from properties not used in CSS attribute selectors: sizes, srcset, border-radius, fallback-src, position.

findings.title: noHeader and noFooter properties use reflect: true unnecessarily
findings.description: The noHeader and noFooter boolean properties both use reflect: true. These properties control conditional rendering inside the shadow DOM template only.
findings.impact: Unnecessary DOM attribute writes for internal rendering flags.
findings.fix: Check if :host([no-header]) or :host([no-footer]) CSS selectors exist. If not, remove reflect: true.

findings.title: position property with reflect: true updates DOM attribute on every drag frame
findings.description: The 'position' property has reflect: true, meaning during a drag operation, the position attribute is written to the DOM on every pointermove event (60+ times per second).
findings.impact: DOM attribute write 60+ times per second during drag.
findings.fix: Remove reflect: true from position. Only reflect when the drag ends.

findings.title: Slot tracking uses plain properties with manual requestUpdate() calls
findings.description: hx-text-input tracks slot content via plain boolean properties (_hasLabelSlot, _hasErrorSlot, _hasPrefixSlot, _hasSuffixSlot, _hasHelpTextSlot) and calls this.requestUpdate() manually in each slot change handler. Using @state() decorators would be cleaner and more idiomatic. The current pattern works correctly but obscures reactivity tracking -- developers reading the code cannot tell these are reactive without examining each handler.
findings.impact: Low runtime impact. Code maintainability concern -- 5 manual requestUpdate() calls that could be automatic.
findings.fix: Convert _hasLabelSlot, _hasErrorSlot, _hasPrefixSlot, _hasSuffixSlot, _hasHelpTextSlot to @state() properties and remove the requestUpdate() calls.

findings.title: Inline arrow function closures in render template
findings.description: The checkbox render template contains two inline arrow functions: `@click=${(e: Event) => { e.preventDefault(); e.stopPropagation(); }}` and `@change=${(e: Event) => e.stopPropagation()}` on lines 313-317. These create new function objects on every render, preventing Lit from short-circuiting the event listener binding.
findings.impact: Two new function allocations per render cycle. Low individual impact but pattern should be avoided.
findings.fix: Extract to class methods: private _preventInputClick(e: Event) { e.preventDefault(); e.stopPropagation(); } and private _stopChangePropagation(e: Event) { e.stopPropagation(); }

findings.title: _getDisplayLines() and _isTruncated() both split the same string
findings.description: Both _getDisplayLines() and _isTruncated() independently call this._codeText.split('\n'). In render(), both are called: `const displayLines = this._getDisplayLines()` and `const truncated = this._isTruncated()`. This results in the code text being split into an array twice per render.
findings.impact: Redundant string split operation. For large code blocks, this allocates two identical arrays.
findings.fix: Cache the split lines array and derive both display lines and truncation status from it. Or pass the lines count to _isTruncated: `private _isTruncated(lines: string[]): boolean { return this.maxLines > 0 && lines.length > this.maxLines; }`

findings.title: Math.random() used for panel ID instead of monotonic counter
findings.description: hx-overflow-menu uses Math.random() to generate its panel ID, unlike every other component in the library which uses SSR-safe monotonic counters. Math.random() is not deterministic across SSR/hydration boundaries and causes hydration mismatches when the server and client generate different IDs.
findings.impact: SSR hydration mismatch. Inconsistent with codebase conventions.
findings.fix: Replace with a module-level monotonic counter: let _overflowMenuCounter = 0; ... this._panelId = `hx-overflow-menu-panel-${++_overflowMenuCounter}`;

findings.title: Keyboard handler queries all accordion items' shadow DOMs on every keydown
findings.description: The _handleKeyDown method in hx-accordion calls querySelectorAll to find all hx-accordion-item children, then for each one accesses its shadowRoot to find the summary element for focus management. This traversal happens on every ArrowUp/ArrowDown keypress.
findings.impact: Shadow root traversal for each item on every keyboard navigation event. Typically only 5-10 items so impact is low.
findings.fix: Cache the focusable summary elements and invalidate on slotchange. Low priority since accordion item counts are typically small.

findings.title: _hideBackgroundFromScreenReaders iterates all document.body children on every open
findings.description: When the drawer opens, _hideBackgroundFromScreenReaders iterates all direct children of document.body to set aria-hidden. While this is necessary for the inert-like pattern, it runs on every open and restores on every close.
findings.impact: Iterates body.children on every open/close. Typically < 20 elements, so low impact.
findings.fix: This is an acceptable implementation. The only optimization would be to skip if already in the correct state. Low priority.

findings.title: _files state creates new array on every setProgress call
findings.description: The setProgress() method creates a new _files array via spread + map on every progress update. For file uploads with frequent progress events, this creates many intermediate arrays that are immediately discarded.
findings.impact: Array allocation on every progress event. Low impact since progress events are typically throttled.
findings.fix: This is idiomatic Lit state management (immutable updates). The impact is low. No change recommended unless profiling shows a bottleneck.

findings.title: SVG star render methods create new template results per call
findings.description: The _renderFilledStar(), _renderEmptyStar(), and _renderHalfStar() methods return new html template results on every call. Since the SVG paths are static, these could be module-level constants like hx-accordion-item's chevronIcon pattern.
findings.impact: Minor: Lit caches template results efficiently, so the overhead is the function call + template creation, not DOM recreation.
findings.fix: Extract SVG templates to module-level constants: const filledStar = html`<svg>...</svg>`; Low priority.

findings.title: Vite build does not use preserveModules for npm output
findings.description: The Vite config uses per-component entry points (good) but does not set preserveModules: true. Without this, Rollup may merge shared code into chunks that bundle more code than needed for individual component imports.
findings.impact: Shared chunks may include code from unused components.
findings.fix: Consider adding preserveModules: true for npm output. Evaluate tradeoff with CDN single-bundle requirement.

findings.title: @floating-ui/dom imported eagerly by 5 components
findings.description: @floating-ui/dom (~3KB min+gz) is imported at module level by hx-popup, hx-popover, hx-tooltip, hx-dropdown, and hx-overflow-menu. Since it is externalized as a peer dependency, this does not affect the library bundle size directly.
findings.impact: Peer dependency required for 5 components. Acceptable with per-component imports.
findings.fix: Acceptable as-is. Document that consumers using only non-popup components do not need to install @floating-ui/dom.

findings.title: SVG sort icon rendered inline in template on every header render
findings.description: The _renderSortIcon method includes a full inline SVG element in the template. For each sortable column header, Lit creates this SVG template on every render.
findings.impact: Minor template overhead per sortable column.
findings.fix: Extract to a module-level constant. Low priority.

findings.title: hx-color-picker is the largest component at 964 lines
findings.description: At 964 lines of TypeScript (plus styles), hx-color-picker is likely the largest individual component. The minified+gzipped size may approach or exceed the 5KB per-component budget.
findings.impact: Potential budget violation. Needs measurement.
findings.fix: Measure actual min+gz size. If over budget: (1) Extract color-utils.ts, (2) Lazy-load eye-dropper support, (3) Split into core picker and optional panels.

findings.title: hx-date-picker is 1019 lines, second largest component
findings.description: At 1019 lines, hx-date-picker includes date arithmetic, calendar grid rendering, keyboard navigation, localization, and form participation.
findings.impact: Potential budget violation. Needs measurement.
findings.fix: Measure actual min+gz size. If over budget, extract date arithmetic utilities.

findings.title: hx-combobox is 851 lines, third largest component
findings.description: At 851 lines, hx-combobox includes filtering logic, multi-select support, keyboard navigation, form association, and dropdown management. Combined with its floating-ui dependency, the total consumer-facing size may be significant.
findings.impact: Potential budget violation. Needs measurement.
findings.fix: Measure actual min+gz size.

findings.title: Document click listener always active
findings.description: hx-time-picker registers a document click listener in connectedCallback that is always active, even when the dropdown is closed. The handler checks if the dropdown is open before acting, but the listener itself fires on every document click.
findings.impact: Document click handler fires on every page click. Low overhead per instance.
findings.fix: Register only when dropdown opens, remove when it closes. Low priority since the early-return guard minimizes overhead.

findings.title: Document click listener always active when component is in DOM
findings.description: hx-select registers a document click listener in connectedCallback for outside-click detection. Like hx-time-picker, this is always active regardless of dropdown state.
findings.impact: Document click handler per select instance. Pages with many selects accumulate handlers.
findings.fix: Register only when dropdown opens. Low priority due to early-return guard.

findings.title: Arrow function closures in carousel render template
findings.description: The carousel render template uses `@click=${() => this.previous()}` and `@click=${() => this.next()}` which create new function objects on every render. The carousel SVG icons are correctly extracted as module-level constants (good pattern), but the click handlers are not.
findings.impact: Two function allocations per render. Very low impact since carousel rarely re-renders.
findings.fix: Use bound method references: @click=${this.previous} and @click=${this.next}. Low priority.

positivePatterns.description: SVG icons extracted as module-level tagged template constants. This avoids recreating template results on every render and allows Lit to efficiently reuse the cached template.

These components cache expensive computed values (_cachedTicks, _buildPageRange cache key, _cachedSlots) and only recompute when input properties change. This is the correct pattern for derived state.
These components cache querySelectorAll results (_cachedTabs, _cachedPanels, _cachedRadios, _focusableCache) and invalidate on slotchange. This avoids redundant DOM queries.
Module-level monotonic counters (++counter) for unique IDs instead of Math.random(). This ensures IDs are deterministic across SSR/hydration boundaries.
Document-level listeners properly added in connectedCallback and removed in disconnectedCallback. hx-number-input correctly clears long-press interval/timer in disconnectedCallback.
Using willUpdate() instead of updated() for property validation and derived state computation. This runs before render without scheduling a second update cycle.
Using @query decorator for cached shadow DOM element references instead of repeated querySelector calls.
The package.json exports field provides per-component entry points (./components/*), allowing consumers to import individual components without pulling in the entire library.
